text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Michael(x) ::: x is Michael.
Windy(x) ::: x is Windy.
Shooter(x) ::: x is a shooter.
Class(x) ::: x is in Michael's class.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) ∀y (Class(y) → Taller(Michael, y)) ::: Michael is taller than everyone in his class.
Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z) → Taller(x, z) ::: If x is taller than y and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
Blocks(Michael, y) ← ¬Jumps(y) ::: Michael can block y's shooting if y does not jump.
¬Blocks(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
Jumps(x) → GreatShooter(x) ::: Shooters who jump are great shooters.
Conclusion:
Peter is shorter than a man in Michael's class.
